source.title: Pre-trained Large Language Models Learn Hidden Markov Models In-context
source.authors: Yijia Dai; Zhaolin Gao; Yahya Sattar; Sarah Dean; Jennifer J. Sun

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices and checklist; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests model-size differences in performance on an in-context HMM prediction task, a different setting and measure from the original pretraining-loss scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper measures ICL prediction accuracy and Hellinger distance against context length, and compares several pretrained model sizes. It does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy against parameter count, tokens, or compute; fit power laws; test small-run extrapolation; or find a compute-optimal allocation. Context-length results are related but do not match a listed version.
record.test_reason: The main results vary context length, not model scale. One appendix ablation (E.1, Figs 15–20) compares seven pretrained Qwen/Llama models (0.5B–8B) on the HMM ICL task. It gives a weak, qualitative new-setting result on whether downstream performance improves with model size. No loss, power-law fit, extrapolation or allocation is studied.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that pretrained LLMs approach Viterbi-optimal HMM prediction via ICL and outperform Baum-Welch, LSTM and similar baselines. They add that 'in-context scaling trends' with context length depend on entropy and mixing rate, and that ICL competes with expert models on mouse decision data. They cite Kaplan only to frame context-length trends as a scaling law. They draw no conclusions about pretraining-loss scaling; model size gets only a brief note that performance is similar, with slight small-model degradation.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates pretrained LLMs in-context on synthetic and real-world sequential prediction tasks, varying context length and comparing model sizes; it does not conduct pretraining runs or fit held-out loss scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported ICL results vary with context length and HMM entropy and mixing rate; the paper also reports differences by model size, tokenization, and the information included in the input sequence.

fits_no_version.finding: Qwen2.5-7B ICL accuracy on HMM sequences improves roughly monotonically with context length (4–2048) before plateauing. Hellinger distance mostly decreases. Convergence is slower with higher entropy and slower mixing, and unaffected by state count at fixed normalized entropy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context (context-length) scaling of prediction performance on stochastic sequences is shaped by process entropy and mixing rate.

record.problems: The model-size comparison is qualitative in the text and is shown for selected HMM configurations; the main performance measure is HMM ICL accuracy rather than held-out pretraining loss. The study does not examine parameter/token/compute power-law fits or compute-optimal training splits.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-version-matched results. The context-length findings are represented by aggregate textual results, rather than extracting individual values from the numerous figure-only curves in Figures 3–5 and 9–22.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No power-law fit in another modality or training regime.
No fitted scale or loss-to-task rule; only a qualitative 0.5B–8B comparison on one synthetic task family.
No fitted exponents or fitting-choice comparison.

missing.what: Condition dependence of the model-size effect. Smallest models are suboptimal 'especially when mixing is fast' (Fig 17). Models converge similarly at high entropy (Fig 16) and slow mixing (Fig 18). Small models do poorly at short context under low A and B entropy, which the authors attribute to repeated-n-gram filtering in pretraining (Fig 19).

record.verdict_notes: The record's T2 overstates the link: the paper's 'scaling' is context length, not model resources. Only the appendix size ablation touches V6, and weakly, because the checkpoints come from two families with different training recipes. A researcher might reasonably also treat this study as non-testing (T6 or discusses).

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss sweep against parameters, tokens, or compute.
No fits from small runs are used to predict larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between model size and training tokens is evaluated.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.
The study evaluates ICL on synthetic HMM sequences and animal behavior, but does not test whether the same pretraining-loss power-law form holds across modalities or training regimes.
The model-size comparison concerns HMM ICL task accuracy, not a broad range of downstream benchmarks or performance predicted from pretraining loss; no quantitative prediction rule is fitted.
No fitted parameter/token/compute exponents or compute-optimal allocation are compared across choices, and no parameter-scaling curve is tested for bending.

rows.subject: Seven-model comparison: Qwen2.5-0.5B, Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-3B, Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-3.2-3B, and Llama-3.1-8B
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained; evaluated through ICL without task-specific LLM training
rows.operation_detail: Compared prediction performance across model sizes and families on synthetic HMM sequences.

conditions.value: selected HMM configurations shown in Figures 15 and 16

rows.value: The authors report similar performance overall, with slight degradation for small models; the two smallest models from each family are described as suboptimal.
rows.note: Aggregate qualitative comparison across seven models; the figures show selected configurations, and the text does not provide numeric values for the size comparison.
rows.check: Subject is correct, but this is a cross-family comparison of off-the-shelf checkpoints, not a controlled scale sweep. The text says performances are 'similar, with slight degradation when the model size is small'. Size effects depend on condition: smallest models are worse especially with fast mixing (Fig 17), and models converge similarly at high entropy or slow mixing (Figs 16, 18). No numbers are given.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained; evaluated through ICL without task-specific LLM training
rows.operation_detail: Measured HMM next-observation prediction as context length increased.

conditions.value: 234 HMM settings; 4,096 sequence pairs per parameter configuration

rows.value: Generally improves monotonically with increasing sequence length before plateauing; fluctuations can occur at high sequence entropy.
rows.uncertainty: Performance metrics averaged over 4,096 samples per setting; no error bar stated for this result.
rows.note: Context length is the varied resource, not model parameters, training tokens, or training compute; this result does not test a listed version.
rows.check: Context-length scaling of ICL accuracy. Not a listed version; belongs in fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B

rows.operation_detail: Measured predictive-distribution distance as context length increased.

rows.value: In most cases, the Hellinger distance decreases monotonically with longer context.
rows.locator: Appendix D.4, discussion of Figures 10, 12, and 14
rows.note: This concerns context-length scaling in HMM ICL, not the loss or resource relationships in the listed claim versions.
rows.check: Context-length scaling of Hellinger distance. Not a listed version; belongs in fits_no_version.

relationships.condition: Seven pretrained Qwen2.5/Llama-3 models (0.5B–8B) doing HMM next-observation ICL, λ2=0.75 and varied mixing and steady-state settings
relationships.reason: r1: gains from scale are small and saturate: models are 'similar', and only the two smallest per family are suboptimal. Size differences vanish at high entropy or slow mixing (Figs 16, 18, from the text). So improvement with scale is condition-dependent rather than uniform.
relationships.display_finding: Scale gains were small and saturated, with only the two smallest models per family suboptimal and size differences disappearing at high entropy or slow mixing.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
